# Spectral Flow Cytometry UMAP Analysis

We will create a UMAP from Ope's spectral data. The purpose of this experiment is to recreate the UMAPs generated by Ope in Cafe. If we can generate similar results, this method may give us more control over the analysis. 

## Library and Sample prep


install.packages("BiocManager")

BiocManager::install("FlowSOM")

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(uwot)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(FlowSOM)
library(pheatmap)

data_dir <- "/Data/Input/SpectralFlow_FromOpe_Sorted"

files <- list.files(
  path = data_dir,
  pattern = "\\.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

files
length(files)
```

## Spectral Flow UMAP Analysis

### Extract naming and meta data

```{r}
flow_df <- purrr::map_dfr(files, function(f) {
  
  file_base <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f))
  
  sample_id <- stringr::str_extract(file_base, "Sample\\d+")
  group <- stringr::str_extract(file_base, "Ctrl|CBD")
  
  read.csv(f, check.names = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(
      sample_id = sample_id,
      group = group,
      file_name = basename(f)
    )
})

# Check import
dim(flow_df)
table(flow_df$sample_id, flow_df$group)
colnames(flow_df)
```

### Define markers used in panel.

We can alter this lost if we do not want a marker to define changes in our spectral data. For example, we could remove KI67 if we though its expression was not determining meaningful biology. In this case, our panel is small so we can include everything. 

```{r}
marker_cols <- c(
   "PD1",
  "CD44",
  "CTLA4",
  "CD62L",
  "KI67",
  "FOXP3",
  "CD4",
  "CD8"

)


# Check that all markers exist
setdiff(marker_cols, colnames(flow_df))
```

### Sample QC and Transformations

I noticed in these flow data, the range was determined by the top and bottom 0.1% of the data. We can filter out these huge numbers. 

```{r}
flow_clean <- flow_df

for (m in marker_cols) {
  
  low_cut  <- quantile(flow_clean[[m]], 0.001, na.rm = TRUE)
  high_cut <- quantile(flow_clean[[m]], 0.999, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  flow_clean[[m]] <- pmin(
    pmax(flow_clean[[m]], low_cut),
    high_cut
  )
}
```

Transforming the data is key when a lot of the difference in biology is masked by a non-linear scale. See the below graphs for examples. Changing the cofactor alters the transformation. 

```{r}
flow_trans <- flow_clean

cofactor <- 50

flow_trans[marker_cols] <- asinh(
  flow_trans[marker_cols] / cofactor
)

```

Non-transformed data. See how these graphs have extremely harsh peaks. 
```{r}
flow_df %>%
  select(all_of(marker_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "marker",
    values_to = "expr"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(expr)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100) +
  facet_wrap(~marker, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw()
```

Transformed data shows meaningful differences in marker expression. 
```{r}
flow_trans %>%
  select(all_of(marker_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = "marker",
               values_to = "expr") %>%
  ggplot(aes(expr)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100) +
  facet_wrap(~marker, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
flow_trans %>%
  count(sample_id, group)
```

### Creating UMAP and downsampling

No PCA is necessary because we only have 10 markers. If we had 20-30 markers then we could perform a PCA. 

In this case we used 5000 cells. 

```{r}
set.seed(123)

cells_per_sample <- 2000

flow_ds <- flow_trans %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    
    n_keep <- min(cells_per_sample, nrow(.x))
    
    slice_sample(.x, n = n_keep)
    
  }) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
flow_ds %>%
  count(sample_id, group)
```

### Set UMAP parameters
```{r}
set.seed(123)

umap_mat <- uwot::umap(
  flow_ds[, marker_cols],
  n_neighbors = 30,
  min_dist = 0.15,
  metric = "euclidean",
  verbose = TRUE
)
```
```{r}
flow_umap <- flow_ds %>%
  mutate(
    UMAP_1 = umap_mat[,1],
    UMAP_2 = umap_mat[,2]
  )
```

By group
```{r}
ggplot(flow_umap,
       aes(UMAP_1, UMAP_2, color = group)) +
  geom_point(
    size = 0.15,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```
By sample
```{r}
ggplot(flow_umap,
       aes(UMAP_1, UMAP_2, color = sample_id)) +
  geom_point(
    size = 0.15,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```
By marker
```{r}
flow_umap %>%
  select(
    UMAP_1,
    UMAP_2,
    all_of(marker_cols)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(marker_cols),
    names_to = "marker",
    values_to = "expr"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(UMAP_1, UMAP_2, color = expr)) +
  geom_point(
    size = 0.15,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  facet_wrap(~marker, ncol = 3) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```


### FlowSOM clustering

```{r}
# make numeric matrix for FlowSOM
fsom_input <- flow_ds %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(marker_cols)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

fsom_input[] <- lapply(fsom_input, as.numeric)

fsom_mat <- as.matrix(fsom_input)
```

```{r}
set.seed(123)

fsom <- FlowSOM::FlowSOM(
  fsom_mat,
  colsToUse = seq_len(ncol(fsom_mat)),
  xdim = 10,
  ydim = 10,
  nClus = 6,
  scale = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
# Each cell's SOM node
cell_to_node <- fsom$map$mapping[, 1]

# Each cell's metacluster
flow_umap$cluster <- factor(fsom$metaclustering[cell_to_node])
```

```{r}
ggplot(flow_umap,
       aes(UMAP_1, UMAP_2, color = cluster)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.15, alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

### Dotplot

```{r}
cluster_summary <- flow_umap %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(
    across(all_of(marker_cols), median),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cluster_mat <- cluster_summary %>%
  column_to_rownames("cluster") %>%
  as.matrix()
```

```{r}
cluster_mat_scaled <- scale(cluster_mat)
```

```{r}
pheatmap(
  cluster_mat_scaled,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  fontsize_row = 10,
  fontsize_col = 10,
  angle_col = 45,
  main = "FlowSOM Cluster Marker Heatmap"
)
```
